title: Normalize existing data before deploy, link accounts only after deploy, and guarantee at most one player per user per team with partial unique indexes
decision: Data is handled in two stages. Pre-deploy normalization adds no userId to any document: a document missing status but holding a userId becomes a member with its email cleared; a document missing status with only an email, or with neither, together with every unlinked player carrying a role or an email, becomes an unlinked player with role and email cleared; a member's own stray email is cleared too. Before writing anything, normalization checks for the following and stops, listing the affected documents for the developer, if any occur: a duplicate (teamId, userId); a duplicate invitee email (after lowercasing and trimming) on the same team; a non-member holding the owner role; a team whose count of owner-role members is not exactly one; an invitee or member missing a role; an invitee holding both or neither of userId and email; a userId or teamId that is not an ObjectId; a missing teamId. Normalization finishes by fixing the (teamId, email) index declaration, dropping the plain (teamId, userId) index, creating a partial unique (teamId, userId) index scoped to ObjectId-typed userId, and verifying both indexes' uniqueness and filter through listIndexes. After deploy, normalization is re-run first and its audit confirmed at zero, because ordinary writes from old code during the deploy window can again produce documents that do not fit the model; only then does account linking run: for an INVITED invitation holding only an email, when a case-insensitive exact match via collation resolves to exactly one registered user, a conditional update — matched again on the status and email read — writes that user's id and clears email. It skips writing, and lists the document for the developer, when that user already has a player on the same team, the email matches more than one user, or the invitation changed between the read and the write. Both stages have a read-only audit and a re-runnable script, run by the developer first against the test environment and then production. From then on, inviting an email whose matching user already has a player on that team, or whose unregistered address already has an invitation on that team, returns a conflict error.
context: The 2026-02 unify-player migration created player documents without writing status, and ran $unset status on all of them; the 2026-03 player-invitations migration only added a schema default of NONE, without backfilling. Production had 32 documents with no status. Under the model at the time, an invitation was "has email, no userId," and leaving the team was "clear userId, keep email," so a document missing status with only an email could be a pending invitation or a former member who had left months earlier and still carried their old role — the two could not be told apart reliably. After D41, the repository refuses to read a document that does not fit the model, and existing data still had unlinked players carrying a role or an email (create-player wrote a default role, and writing an email left status at NONE). Some invitations already at INVITED with only an email in fact belonged to an already-registered address, because create-invitation only ever wrote the email and never delivered. The old authorization check passed anyone whose role field existed, without looking at status, so backfilling a userId onto any of these before deploy would let that invitee gain access during the window before deploy. On the index side, the (teamId, email) unique index declared both sparse and a partialFilterExpression, with $nin in the filter, which MongoDB does not accept — it most likely never got created; (teamId, userId) had only an ordinary index, and findByTeamIdAndUserId's findOne would return one of several duplicates at random.

alternatives.option: Derive one of the three shapes at read time for a document missing status
alternatives.reason: Only old documents need this, and the email-only class among them is itself ambiguous; for an ordinary document, an invitee invited first and registered later has fields identical to a member's, which is exactly why status became an explicit field after derivation went wrong once. A read-time derivation would become a permanent special case.

alternatives.option: Keep an old email-only document with no status as an invitee, and link it to a registered account
alternatives.reason: Such a document might be a former member who left months ago, and keeping it as an invitee would send that former member an invitation carrying their old role — possibly admin or owner — months later, with nobody remembering why. Turning it into an unlinked player only costs an admin one re-invite, and matches what the UI has always shown as "not yet invited." The developer initially chose to keep it, then switched to turning it into an unlinked player once the old leave-team behavior was understood.

alternatives.option: Do the backfill and the linking together before deploy
alternatives.reason: The old authorization check looked only at role, so an invitee who got a userId written before deploy would pass the member and admin checks during the pre-deploy window.

alternatives.option: Enforce at most one player per user per team only in application code
alternatives.reason: There is a race between the check and the write, and it does not block other write paths; an application-level check exists to give the user a readable error, while the unique index is what actually guarantees it.

alternatives.option: Auto-resolve a duplicate or a broken invariant when found
alternatives.reason: Which record is correct, and who should be the owner, depends on the team's actual situation; an automatic decision could delete a member's record or change ownership.

consequences: Production must complete normalization before this Change deploys, re-run normalization immediately after deploy, and only then run linking. Running normalization early is safe with respect to authorization, but it does not replace the post-deploy re-run; linking must wait for the new authorization checks to be live.

An old invitation missing status and an unlinked player carrying an email are both withdrawn; an admin can re-invite if still needed. The audit lists their role and last-updated time so the developer can review before running.
An existing invitation that could never be delivered because the address was already registered is now delivered, after deploy.
The database now guarantees at most one player per user per team, and no duplicate invitation to the same email on the same team.
The migration scripts move, at Archive, under docs/changes/archive in this Change's archive directory; their long-term disposition is a separate discussion.
revisitTriggers: A need arises for the same user to hold more than one player on the same team.
The long-term disposition of the archived migration scripts is decided.
